ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. The deviation is real. The GPS trace distance (18.0 km) governs over the receipt's rounded copy, and against the booked optimal of 10.0 km that is 8.0 km / 80% over, so a route deviation is established under POL-RD-01. The trace is not impaired (205 fixes at 10 s, no gaps, 0.0 s max gap), so it stands on its own.

Part of the excess is excused. LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 closes the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector from 18:14 to 18:55, the booked optimal route is recorded as running via that very segment, and the trace leaves and rejoins that corridor - so POL-RD-03 applies. But exoneration is capped at 3.60 km: the lesser of the measured 8.0 km and 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00. That leaves 4.40 km the closure does not excuse, and I have run everything below on the closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km / 27.2 min. The rider's 'please take the lawful diversion' does not move the remaining excess onto the rider as a requested detour: no waypoint_hint is set and no road is named in the rider's instruction, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test could not be run and that clause is unavailable.

The distance refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on the metered fare, surge 1.0 read from the fare breakdown: recomputed fare 23.416, charged total 31.42, refund 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05. The off-route 'Industrial loop exit' ERP of 2.80 is already inside that figure under POL-RD-09(1) - itemised for transparency and not added again.

Separately, and independently of the deviation, the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line is a billing-integrity failure: the trace's nearest fix is 834.18 m, well beyond the 250 m crossing radius, so it charges a gantry the trip never passed. POL-RD-09(4) refunds it in full as a standalone correction and requires it to be recorded and referred. The 'Industrial loop exit' line is not phantom - the trace comes within 223.17 m - so no correction is due on it, and because it is the only other unmatched line, POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 610 completed trips), so neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available. Profile fields not named by a clause (rating, lifetime counters, prior flags) were treated as context only. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across all three instruments, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, the POL-RD-03 advisory is present and covers the window, and the refund is under both charged_total and SGD 150.00.

Total returned to the rider: 8.05 + 1.00 = SGD 9.05. The fare is left otherwise as charged.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line charges a gantry the GPS trace never passes (nearest fix 834.18 m, outside the 250 m crossing radius); refund it in full as a standalone correction and review the fare build.
